subject: Architecture
title: Deconstructivism: Buildings That Break the Rules
description: A quick, practical guide to Deconstructivism: Buildings That Break the Rules.

hook.text: Frank Gehry's Guggenheim Bilbao looks like it's made of crumpled metal — and that's the point.

buildup.text: Deconstructivism rejects straight lines. Walls tilt, roofs fragment, and floors slope on purpose.

discovery.text: Gehry designed the Bilbao museum using aerospace software — the curves were too complex for pencils.

twist.text: Bilbao was a dying industrial city. The museum alone reversed its economy — the 'Bilbao Effect.'

climax.text: Cities worldwide now commission 'starchitect' buildings hoping to replicate that economic miracle.

punchline.text: One weird building saved an entire city. Every mayor noticed.

quiz.question: What is the 'Bilbao Effect'?
options: A structural flaw caused by curved metal panels
An iconic building reviving a city's economy
The tendency for deconstructivist buildings to leak
